h1: Pool and Spa Electrical in Broward County
intro: Water and electricity together demand special protection, and many older South Florida pools no longer have it. Grounding, bonding, and ground fault breakers can quietly fail while everything looks fine. A tripping breaker, a dark light, or a faint tingle on a rail is the warning. We test instead of guess.

definition.heading: What pool and spa electrical work covers
definition.body: Everything on the electrical side of your pool: pump and heater circuits, lighting, the salt system, the breakers, and the grounding and bonding that ties it together. Bonding keeps every metal part at the same electrical level. Grounding gives a fault a safe path so the breaker trips.

symptoms.title: A tingle in the water
symptoms.body: Current is reaching metal it should not, usually a broken bond. It is the clearest warning there is. Get everyone out and have it checked.

symptoms.title: A pool breaker that keeps tripping
symptoms.body: Resetting only buys a little time. On a pool circuit, that breaker is usually sensing a real ground fault and doing exactly its job.

symptoms.title: A pool light out or flickering
symptoms.body: Because the light sits in the water, that is exactly where you want a correct repair rather than a quick guess.

symptoms.title: Your pool still runs on its original breakers
symptoms.body: Fast-tripping ground fault protection may never have been installed, or it has aged out and no longer trips as it should.

localSections.heading: Older South Florida pools, older services, deeper faults
localSections.body: Many South Florida pools date to the 1960s through the 1980s, when bonding standards were looser and some installers used metal conduit as the ground path instead of a wire. Decades of humidity and salt air corrode the lugs, and none of it shows from the deck.

localSections.heading: Permits, inspection, and your insurance in Broward
localSections.body: Broward building departments watch pool electrical closely, which protects you. When a correction needs a permit we pull it, work to current code, and meet the inspector to prove the grounding under test. Some minor fixes do not need one, and we say which is which.

guide.title: The complete guide to pool and spa electrical

sections.heading: Bonding and grounding: two jobs, one safety net
sections.body: Bonding ties every metal part around the pool, rails, ladder, pump, heater, and light niche, into one network, so a swimmer feels no difference in charge between two things they touch at once. Grounding gives fault current a fast path back so the breaker shuts off. The only way to tell a healthy system from a failed one is to test it.

sections.heading: A tripping breaker, and why a pool needs a different one
sections.body: A tripping pool breaker is sensing current escaping the wiring, so never reset it or fit a bigger one. Water lowers the body's resistance, so code calls for a ground fault breaker on the pump, heater, and lighting. A GFCI only protects if it trips, so we test every one before we leave.

sections.heading: When a repair becomes a rebuild
sections.body: Most pool problems are repairs we fix on the spot. A rebuild is different, and the signal is a pattern rather than one fault: fix one circuit and another fails. We once traced a community pool shocking swimmers to metal conduit used as its ground path, and ran new wire with a proper ground.

faqs.question: What is the difference between bonding and grounding?
faqs.answer: Bonding ties all the metal around your pool into one network so everything sits at the same electrical level. Grounding gives fault current a safe path back so the breaker trips. A safe pool needs both.

faqs.question: My pool breaker keeps tripping. Can I just reset it or add a bigger one?
faqs.answer: Please do neither. That breaker is usually sensing a real ground fault and shutting off before the current reaches a swimmer. A bigger one just lets more current flow before protection reacts.

faqs.question: Someone felt a tingle in the pool. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Get everyone out and have it checked before the pool is used again. A tingle means current is reaching metal that is not properly bonded, and the swimmer becomes the path.

faqs.question: How do I know if my pool already has proper ground fault protection?
faqs.answer: A ground fault breaker usually has a small test button, and pressing it should trip the breaker. But a breaker can look correct and still have aged past reliable tripping, so the only way to be sure is to test it.
